findings.evidence: Journaling RW reads are 8,988.2/tick: GetComponentDataRW=2,245.6/tick, GetBufferRW=6,742.7/tick.
findings.inference: The hot path is still shaped around random entity/buffer lookup instead of chunk-local or owner-local batches.
findings.designMistake: Runtime Core modules are too shallow around ability commit, cleanup, and attribute recalculation; callers still pay ECS lookup details every tick.
findings.nextProbe: Split TopN by system and add per-system chunk/entity match counters; prove which paths can move to IJobChunk or owner-local dirty sets.

findings.inference: The data is not suffering from structural changes; it is suffering from a per-command enableable-state protocol.
findings.designMistake: Ability lifecycle is encoded as too many request/commit/end marker flips instead of a compact per-owner command state or chunk batch.
findings.nextProbe: Measure toggle count by component and phase; replace repeated commit/end toggles with a compact command queue state where semantics allow it.

findings.evidence: GAS.Runtime.OwnerLocalGameplayFactBuffer is a hot component RW target: 11,250 records, 1,250.0/tick.
findings.inference: The runtime still pays high buffer RW volume even when structural changes are near zero.
findings.designMistake: Owner-local stores exist, but the execution/attribute/fact path still exposes broad buffer surfaces to too many systems.
findings.nextProbe: Add per-owner dirty counters and prove which TopN component paths can become chunk-local or fixed-width metric streams.

findings.evidence: OwnerLocalFact max owner range is 9; owner-local facts flush 577.8/tick.
findings.inference: The fact path has owner-local storage, but the hot range is still too broad for a strict chunk-local DOTS shape.
findings.designMistake: Fact fan-in is represented as mutable buffers with repeated owner flushes instead of a compact dirty-owner reduction lane.
findings.nextProbe: Add dirty owner/fact span counters and move OwnerLocalGameplayFactBuffer writes behind a generated fact reduce/apply lane.

findings.evidence: OwnerLocalInstant prepare scans 2,400 owners but skips 1,450 (60.4%); promoted commands=0.
findings.inference: The instant command frame lane is sparse at owner granularity.
findings.designMistake: The current prepare system has owner-local buffers but no compact dirty owner read model for frame-local promotion work.
findings.nextProbe: Target generated dirty-owner lanes or owner-local command spans; do not reintroduce enableable marker toggles.

findings.evidence: ActiveMutation prepare scans 2,400 owners but skips 1,750 (72.9%); promoted commands=0.
findings.inference: The active-effect mutation frame lane is sparse at owner granularity.
findings.designMistake: The prepare system still pays broad owner scans for clear/copy even when mutation promotion work is zero.
findings.nextProbe: Use owner-local dirty spans or generated active-effect mutation fan-in before changing query gates.

findings.evidence: Execution scans 1,350 specs for 350 matched effects, ratio=3.86:1.
findings.inference: The execution-calculation path still has fan-out scan cost that grows faster than matched work.
findings.designMistake: Execution definitions are not yet indexed as a compact generated lookup matched to the active gameplay effect command stream.
findings.nextProbe: Generate a calculation-code to effect-spec index and compare spec scan count against matched effect count in the next run.

findings.evidence: DebuggerOwner avg is 179.795 ms for 2,400 materialized entities and 12 queries; GASTick avg is 1.041 ms.
findings.inference: The debugger can locate gameplay hot spots, but its diagnostic materialization/export pass is itself a large one-shot cost.
findings.designMistake: Runtime diagnostics still mix validation evidence, materialization, and text-export obligations too closely.
findings.nextProbe: Keep performance pass counter-only, and split DiagnosticMaterializationPass/export into an explicitly budgeted post-run owner.

findings.evidence: Profiler evidence is missing: performanceExcellentPassed=False, dominantRisk=DependencyWait.
findings.inference: Runtime self-diagnostics and Journaling are enough to find current hot spots, but the official Profiler leg is not enabled.
findings.designMistake: The validation contract now distinguishes headless budget pass from DOTS-profiler-backed performance excellence, but the runner still defaults to disabled Profiler.
findings.nextProbe: Add an explicit profiler-enabled validation mode or record a hard reason why batchmode Profiler is unavailable on this machine.
